title: Sherpa is alive after a week on Mount Everest

paragraphs: A 52-year-old mountain guide named Dawa Sherpa went missing on Mount Everest for a week. He was high up on the world’s tallest mountain, where it is very cold and there is not enough air to breathe.

His family thought he was dead, so his wife and young daughter started a traditional funeral at home. But then, a miracle happened. A rescue team saw Dawa crawling in the snow near the base camp. He couldn’t walk, and his hands were hurt by the extreme cold, but he was alive. The team gave him food and water, and a helicopter took him to a hospital. His daughter said they were very happy but shocked when they saw photos of their father in the local news.
People say he survived because mountain guides in Nepal are very strong and know how to live in bad weather.

paragraphs: A 52-year-old Nepali mountain guide, Dawa Sherpa, was miraculously found alive after being missing for nearly a week on Mount Everest.
He was last seen on May 29 in the dangerous death zone near the top of the mountain, where he stayed behind to let others descend during bad weather.

When he didn’t return, his family and the climbing community believed he had died. In fact, his wife and teenage daughter had already started traditional funeral rituals at home. However, six days later, a support team spotted Dawa crawling down the snowy slopes near Everest Base Camp. Although he suffered from frostbite on his hands, he was in surprisingly good health. He was immediately given food and water and airlifted by helicopter to a hospital in Kathmandu.

His daughter explained that when they first heard the local news, they couldn’t believe it and had to ask for photos to be sure it was really their father. Experts called his survival a true miracle, even though Sherpas are incredibly strong and familiar with the harsh mountain environment.
